options: A row whose real-world event timestamp is significantly earlier than when it actually arrived in bronze
Any row that arrives after 5pm local time
A row that fails schema enforcement
Any row processed by a job cluster instead of an all-purpose cluster
questions.explain: The trip's tpep_pickup_datetime and its _ingested_at (Lesson 26) being meaningfully different is the definition.

questions.q: Why does a naive gold aggregate break when data arrives late?
options: A published number for a past date can already be wrong, missing a trip that genuinely belongs to that date but hadn't arrived yet when gold was computed
Late data always causes a schema mismatch error
Gold tables cannot be updated once written
Late data is automatically rejected by Delta's schema enforcement
questions.explain: A pipeline that only ever processes "today's new rows" will never notice or fix this missing trip.

questions.q: How does reprocessing a lookback window address late-arriving data?
options: It recomputes gold for a window of recent dates (not just the current day), catching late records that trickled in for those dates
It deletes all late-arriving rows from bronze automatically
It only works if the late data arrives within one hour
It requires rebuilding the entire gold table from the very beginning every time
questions.explain: A 2-3 day lookback window is a practical compromise between always-correct and recomputing everything forever.

questions.q: What role does MERGE play in fixing late-arriving data's effect on gold?
options: It corrects already-published gold numbers for the affected dates, replacing just those rows with recomputed values
MERGE cannot be used to fix gold tables, only silver ones
MERGE deletes the late-arriving rows entirely
MERGE is unrelated to this problem; only OPTIMIZE addresses it
questions.explain: This is the same MERGE from Lesson 22, now doing genuinely different work: correction rather than deduplication.

questions.q: Why does bronze's append-only, never-filtering design (Lesson 26) matter for handling late data?
options: Late data is still just another row landing in bronze on its own schedule — nothing about the pipeline design has to change to "support" it
Bronze must be redesigned specifically to accept late-arriving rows
Late data is rejected by bronze and must be manually re-inserted
Bronze's design has no relationship to how late data gets handled
questions.explain: This is the real payoff of bronze never assuming perfectly on-time arrival in the first place.
